# Pinned OMP 19.1.0 package inputs

The twelve core archives in this directory are the official npm archives for OMP 19.1.0, revision `a7135b8f31826c878734388b648f52bed8da436e`. Keep the archive bytes unchanged. [The copy manifest](copy-manifest.json) records source URLs, sizes and digests, including the six platform-specific native leaves. The leaves resolve from npm rather than Git; Docker and Electron consume the same pinned closure.

Root `patchedDependencies` applies the existing third-party patches and the application SDK patch to the vendored archive. The SDK patch retains offline initial model discovery and Bash job observation; it also preserves explicitly configured tool-command settings under their new names, authorizes native Bash at execution without replacing the built-in — including a process-wide `requireBashExecutionAuthorization()` fail-closed switch a host process sets once so a Bash tool without a session authorizer throws instead of running —, routes special commands through the registered tool policy wrapper, and backports [OMP PR 20113](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20113) for MCP negotiation fallback. Host-mediation seams extend the same boundary: `CreateAgentSessionOptions.authorizeModelUse` wraps the session model registry in a mediated proxy (`config/mediated-model-registry.ts`) so every credential mint inside the session — primary-turn resolution, compaction and context-promotion probes, recovery fallback probes, job-widget captioning, branch summaries and ephemeral side turns — authorizes with the host first, throwing a distinguishable `HostModelUseRefusedError` whose refusal the candidate loops skip per candidate and surface verbatim when no authorized candidate remains; prompt preflight alone probes credential existence through `unmediatedModelRegistry` because it must not consume the turn's authorization. Remote memory embeddings are a provider use of their own purpose: `authorizeEmbeddingUse` authorizes the exact embedding provider/model/endpoint tuple with `purpose: "embedding"` before mnemopi mints its OpenRouter resolver or any pinned or environment key may ride a remote embedding request, and the gates are fail-closed: `allowRemote` passes only for an admitted use at the admitted endpoint (never-authorized equals refused), keys are minted only after admission and pinned explicitly so no env credential can ride a non-admitted use, and a refusal is reported once through the session notice path while local fastembed embeddings keep working; the embedding resolver mint itself uses `unmediatedModelRegistry` because a provider-scoped resolution through the chat-mediation path would authorize an empty model id and always be refused. The effective endpoint — resolved exactly as core resolves it, env fallback included — is pinned into the runtime options so core cannot re-resolve, the `allowRemote` gate admits only that endpoint, and `/memory clear` rehydrates through the same mediated resolution; the remote extraction LLM authorizes as an exact chat tuple the same way. The wrap covers inherited spawns (structured subagents, vibe workers, persisted revivals and advisors), and `runCleanse`/`createCleanseAgentRuntime` accept an optional `host` context that reuses the host's settings, auth storage, model registry, credential resolver, bash authorizer and prepared extensions — no fresh discovery or online refresh — and mediates every checker executable spawn through `authorizeCheckerCommand` before it starts.

The npm archive omits the browser relay extension workspace. The SDK patch keeps the native messaging host identifier in the package so that importing the SDK does not require that unpublished workspace.

To refresh artifacts, verify the official npm provenance and integrity for the target release; compare archive sizes and SHA-256 against the manifest. Update the root and service manifests, lockfile, Docker inputs and desktop staging checks together. Verify the SDK patch against a pristine extraction of the coding-agent archive before installing.
